header.running_head: The Lectures of Hadhrat Utba bin Ghazwaan (RA)

blocks.text: tore it into two parts. I used one part as a lower garment for myself and the other I gave to Sa'd bin Maalik, who also used it as a loincloth. However, today there is none of us who has not become the governor of a city. I ask Allaah to protect me from standing high in my own esteem while being humiliated in Allaah's sight." [^1]

Another narration adds that Hadhrat Utba (RA) concluded with the words, "There has never been a (succession of leaders starting from the period of) Nabuwwaat that does not gradually decline until it degenerates into a monarchy. After me you shall soon experience and be tested with many (different types) of leaders and governors (so prepare yourselves)." [^2]

Yet another narration states that this was the first lecture that Hadhrat Utba (RA) delivered in Basrah. He said, "All praise belongs to Allaah Whom I praise, from Whom I seek help, Who I believe in and in Whom do I rely. I testify that there is none worthy of worship but Allaah and I testify that Muhammad ﷺ is the servant and Rasul of Allaah. O people! Verily this world has already..." The rest of the narration is like both narrations quoted above. [^3]
The Lectures of Hadhrat Hudhayfah bin Yamaan (RA)

Hadhrat Abu Abdur Rahmaan Sulami reports, "I once accompanied my father for the Jumu'ah salaah in Madaa'in. We lived a Farsakh away from the Masjid and it was during the time when Hadhrat Hudhayfah bin Yamaan (RA) was the governor of Madaa'in. He ascended the pulpit and after praising Allaah, he recited the verse:
Qiyaamah has drawn close and the moon has been split.

He then continued, 'Listen well! The moon has already been split. Listen well! This world has already announced her departure. Listen well! Today (this world) is the time for the race while tomorrow it will be seen who has gone ahead.' I then asked my father, 'What does he mean by the race?' My father informed me that he was referring to the race to Jannah." [^4]
Another similar narration states that Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) said, "Allaah says:
Qiyaamah has drawn close and the moon has been split.
